_about: Every word the trading calendar shows: holiday names, tag names and notes, each market's note for a kind of day, and the playbook lines. Placeholders: {holiday} is today's holiday, {next_holiday} the one the market is about to close for, {next_open} the next stock session open in New York time. Seasonal notes describe tendencies in past data, never forecasts.

holiday.name: Market holiday
holiday.label: {holiday}: stocks closed
holiday.note: {holiday}: US stocks and options are shut all day. They open again {next_open}.

weekend.name: Weekend
weekend.label: Weekend: crypto only
weekend.note: US stocks and options are shut until {next_open}. Coins trade on thinner books; futures and forex reopen Sunday evening.

half_day.name: Half day
half_day.label: Half day: closes 1 PM
half_day.note: Stocks close at 1 PM New York, index options at 1:15. Volume is thin.

triple_witching.name: Triple witching
triple_witching.label: Triple witching
triple_witching.note: Stock options, index options and index futures all expire today. Heavy volume, most of it at the open and the close.

monthly_expiry.name: Monthly options expiry
monthly_expiry.label: Monthly options expiry
monthly_expiry.note: Monthly stock and index options expire today: the third Friday, or the Thursday before when that Friday is a holiday.

pre_holiday.name: Last session before a holiday
pre_holiday.label: Last session before {next_holiday}
pre_holiday.note: The market is shut next for {next_holiday}. Whatever is held at the close is held through the closed day.

year_end.name: Last session of the year
year_end.label: Last session of the year
year_end.note: Funds close their books for the year: rebalancing and window dressing move prices into the close.

quarter_end.name: Quarter end
quarter_end.label: Quarter end
quarter_end.note: The last session of the quarter: funds rebalance and dress their books, so late moves can be flows, not news.

month_end.name: Month end
month_end.label: Month end
month_end.note: The last session of the month: pension and fund rebalancing shows up late in the day.

quarter_start.name: First session of the quarter
quarter_start.label: First session of the quarter
quarter_start.note: New quarter, new books: fresh money is put to work and last quarter's window dressing comes off.

month_start.name: First session of the month
month_start.label: First session of the month
month_start.note: Monthly contributions arrive: the first session often runs on flows rather than news.

vix_expiry.name: VIX expiration
vix_expiry.label: VIX expiration
vix_expiry.note: VIX futures and options settle this morning. Volatility readings are noisy around the open.

first_day_back.name: First session back
first_day_back.label: First session back
first_day_back.note: The first session after a weekend or a holiday: news from the closed days is priced at the open.

friday.name: Friday
friday.label: Friday: weeklies expire
friday.note: Weekly options expire at the close, and Fridays lean toward selling: few want to carry risk through two closed days. A tendency, not a rule. A stock or option sold today is Monday's money in a cash account.

santa_rally.name: Santa Claus rally window
santa_rally.note: A tendency, not a forecast: the last five sessions of the year and the first two of the next have risen more often than not. Small sample, thin volume.

thanksgiving_week.name: Thanksgiving week
thanksgiving_week.note: Thursday is closed and Friday is a half day. Volume is light all week, so a move on a thin tape means less.

earnings_season.name: Earnings season
earnings_season.note: Roughly the four weeks when most large companies report. Stocks gap on results and option prices deflate once a report is out. These dates are approximate: each company's own date is on the news calendar.

post_midterm.name: Post-midterm window
post_midterm.note: A tendency, not a forecast: November to June after a US midterm election has been a favorable stretch for the S&P 500 historically. Context for risk posture, not a signal and not a trade (notes/strategy-evals.md).

january_effect.name: January effect
january_effect.note: A tendency, not a forecast: small stocks sold for tax losses in December have often bounced in January. Weaker in recent decades.

september.name: September
september.note: A tendency, not a forecast: historically the weakest month for US stocks on average. Plenty of Septembers rise.

sell_in_may.name: Sell in May half
sell_in_may.note: A tendency, not a forecast: May through October has been the weaker half of the year historically, and the effect has faded in recent decades. Weaker is not the same as down.

summer_doldrums.name: Summer doldrums
summer_doldrums.note: A tendency, not a forecast: August volume is usually the lightest of the year. Thin markets drift, then jump.

tax_loss_selling.name: Tax-loss selling
tax_loss_selling.note: A tendency, not a forecast: the year's losers often see extra selling in November and December as holders book losses for taxes.

cycle_post_election.name: Post-election year
cycle_post_election.note: Year one of the four-year US presidential cycle. Historically mixed, on a small sample. A tendency, not a forecast.

cycle_midterm.name: Midterm year
cycle_midterm.note: Year two of the four-year US presidential cycle. Historically the choppiest of the four, on a small sample. A tendency, not a forecast.

cycle_pre_election.name: Pre-election year
cycle_pre_election.note: Year three of the four-year US presidential cycle. Historically the strongest of the four, on a small sample. A tendency, not a forecast.

cycle_election.name: Election year
cycle_election.note: Year four of the four-year US presidential cycle. Markets have tended to trade nervously into November. A tendency, not a forecast.

stocks.open: Regular session 9:30 AM to 4 PM New York.
stocks.half: Opens 9:30 AM, closes early at 1 PM New York.
stocks.weekend: Closed for the weekend. Opens {next_open} New York.

options.open: Trade with the stock session, 9:30 AM to 4 PM New York.
options.half: Close early with stocks at 1 PM New York; index options at 1:15.
options.weekend: Closed with stocks. Time value still drains over the weekend.
options.holiday: Closed with stocks for {holiday}. Time value still drains while they are shut.

futures.open: CME futures trade nearly round the clock, with a one-hour break at 5 PM New York.
futures.friday: CME futures close at 5 PM New York for the weekend.
futures.saturday: Closed. CME futures reopen Sunday at 6 PM New York.
futures.sunday: Closed until 6 PM New York, then open into Monday.
futures.holiday: Holiday hours: shortened or paused. Check the exchange before trusting a quote.

forex.open: Around the clock. Busiest when London and New York overlap, 8 AM to noon New York.
forex.friday: Closes at 5 PM New York for the weekend.
forex.saturday: Closed until Sunday 5 PM New York.
forex.sunday: Closed until 5 PM New York, then open into Monday.
forex.holiday: Trades on a US holiday schedule: thin, with wide spreads. Check your broker's hours.

crypto.thin: Never closes, but books are thinner while banks and CME are shut. Moves run further on less money.

prediction.always: Kalshi and Polymarket never close. Each contract settles on its own event's clock.

holiday: Stocks and options are shut for {holiday}: only coins trade. Half size, books are thin.
Nothing settles today: the last session's sales become cash at the next open.
weekend: Stocks and options are shut: only coins trade. Half size, books are thin.
Use the quiet to read the week ahead: earnings, Fed, expiries.
Friday's stock and option sales are not cash yet: they settle at Monday's open.
half_day: Closes at 1 PM. Volume is thin: smaller size, exits by noon.
A thin tape gaps through a stop more easily: size for the gap, not for the stop.
triple_witching: Three kinds of contract expire together: the volume is real, but it says nothing about direction.
No new option plays that expire today. Anything expiring is out before the last hour.
monthly_expiry: Positions pin and unpin around big strikes. No new option plays that expire today.
A play expiring today leaves on its time exit, never at the bell.
pre_holiday: A cash account carries nothing through a closed day it would not hold for three.
Options lose the closed days' time value while nobody can trade them: check every exit before the bell.
year_end: Funds dress their books into the close: a late move can be flows, not news.
quarter_end: Funds rebalance into the close: a late move can be flows, not news.
month_end: Month-end flows move prices late in the day with no headline behind them.
quarter_start: New money on the first session: let volume confirm a move before following it.
month_start: New money on the first session: let volume confirm a move before following it.
vix_expiry: VIX contracts settle at the open: do not read the first hour's volatility as news.
first_day_back: The open prices in everything that happened while the market was shut. Wait out the first 15 minutes.
A gap is not a signal. Volume after the first half hour is.
friday: Nothing is carried into the weekend on hope: it has its stop and its time exit, or it is closed.
What is sold today is Monday's money: it settles at the next open.
normal: A normal session. The rulebook as written.
Every play has its stop, its ladder and its time exit before it has a dollar in it.
events: Scheduled events (Fed, CPI, jobs, earnings) are on the news service's calendar: newsd /api/calendar.
